why: All three checks pass. (1) The sentence exists VERBATIM at memory.md:99 of the curl'd page. The whole line is two sentences and the second REINFORCES rather than reverses: 'Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks. To mention a path in your CLAUDE.md without importing it, wrap it in backticks: writing `` `@README` `` keeps the text literal, while `@README` outside backticks imports the file.' The page is row 44 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a valid Claude contract citation. (2) The cited code says what was claimed. parseMemoryImportPath (memory-store.ts:49-64) takes a single line with no surrounding state; readMemoryFileWithImports (memory-store.ts:82-107) iterates raw.split(/\r?\n/) and hands each line to it; native-sources.ts:427-429 does the same inside memoryFileRecords' visit(). A repo-wide `grep -a` for fenced/code-span state (inCodeBlock, fenceState, insideFence, codeSpan) finds implementations only in packages/ui/src/components/markdown/linkify.ts, packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-context.ts and packages/shared/src/labels/auto/evaluator.ts -- none in the memory-import path. (3) The CONSEQUENCE was verified separately from the identifier, by execution, not by reading. A temporary bun test wrote a MEMORY.md containing a ```text fence whose body line is `@secret.md`, then called loadMemoryPromptBlock(undefined, undefined, {userConfigDir: tmp}). Output: the <memory> block contains ```text / SECRET_IMPORTED_BODY / ``` -- the fenced line was followed and the imported file inlined INSIDE the fence. Nothing upstream strips fences (readMemoryFile only reads and slices to MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT), so the 'enforcement one layer up' shape does not apply. The probe also confirmed the claim's parenthetical: parseMemoryImportPath('`@README`') and ('`@docs/x.md`') both return null, purely as a side effect of the trimmed-startsWith('@') gate. Not a recorded owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 concerns memory imports, the deviation register has no import row, and the coverage map's 9 recorded memory.md deviations do not include this. Not a rebrand or a dropped-subscription product difference either -- MEMORY.md import following is a shipped feature that simply lacks the documented markdown-awareness.
correctedState: Confirmed, with three corrections to scope. (a) There are THREE parseMemoryImportPath call sites, not two: memory-store.ts:83 (the inlining walker), capabilities/native-sources.ts:428 (the capability-record walker, which additionally registers the fenced target as its own NativeCapabilitySourceRecord with memoryImportParentPath), and agent/base-agent.ts:1005, which filters import lines OUT of the pinned capability body -- so on the capability-runtime route a fenced `@path` line is deleted from inside the code block instead of inlined. Every one of the three is stateless per line; the fenced code block is corrupted on both routes. (b) Name the subsystem: this is the MEMORY.md / .agents/rules / .claude/rules import walker. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md project instruction files are registered by fileRecord('instruction', ...) (native-sources.ts, PROJECT_INSTRUCTION_FILES) and are NOT import-walked at all, so the fence question does not arise there -- the separate and larger divergence is that instruction files support no `@` imports in any position. (c) The code-span half is wider than 'a backtick-wrapped @README at line start happens to be rejected': because the gate is line.trim().startsWith('@'), NO code span anywhere is ever followed -- but neither is any legitimate mid-line import, and memory.md:101 says to 'reference them with `@` syntax anywhere in your CLAUDE.md'. Verified: parseMemoryImportPath('See @README for x') === null. So the code-span rule is satisfied only by also violating the anywhere-in-the-line rule; the single real gap is a fenced-block line whose trimmed start is `@<path>`.
